framing_issues.text: If you care most about transparency and informed decision-making: Commissioner Dana Barrett, who sponsored Option C
framing_issues.issue: Uneven values guide. Its only entry pairs "transparency" with Option C, which the Board had already set aside. Yet Ellis claims transparency for the current process: "more transparent and open than anything we've had in recent years" (P-073). The guide also leaves out the other documented priorities: balanced north/south input (P-004), and the justice officials' calls for more money and a January vote (P-070). A reader who values openness is steered to one side. Note that both sides claim transparency, or add parallel lines for the other documented values.

framing_issues.text: Whether your 2027 county property tax changes isn't known yet, as of Nov 8, 2026, because the proposal isn't public.
framing_issues.issue: This sentence appears alone on the home page and gives the wrong main reason. Tax bills depend on the millage rate and property values (P-102), and the rate is set separately, after the budget (P-098, P-101). Readers may expect the Nov 15 proposal to answer the tax question.

framing_issues.text: The proposal, due by Nov 15, wasn't public then
framing_issues.issue: "Isn't/wasn't public" (also lines 15, 36, 133, 139, 141, 149, 241) is stated as fact. The evidence is only that the proposal was not on the county's budget page on Nov 8 (P-045).

framing_issues.text: In general, a consent decree is a legal settlement that a court approves and can enforce.
framing_issues.issue: Missing context that may mislead. The sources call it an "agreement with the United States Department of Justice" (P-048) and never say a court approved it. The definition invites readers to assume court approval and enforcement.

framing_issues.text: to address conditions at the county jail
framing_issues.issue: Softens P-048's "to address constitutional violations at the Fulton County Jail". The definition also sits inside "What's uncertain", which is confusing.

framing_issues.text: The District 4 seat is vacant, so people there can contact the chairman.
framing_issues.issue: Missing context: on the Budget Commission, the Southern Representative (Vice Chair Abdur-Rahman) represents districts 4 to 6, which include District 4 (P-008, P-013).

framing_issues.text: Johnson said ... Commissioner Dana Barrett said the two are "creating a budget commission that only they qualify to be on."
framing_issues.issue: Uneven attribution in the cards. Paraphrases name FOX 5, but direct quotes from Atlanta News First (Barrett at lines 178, 188; Ellis at lines 190, 211-212) name no outlet. Readers can't tell which report each quote came from.

framing_issues.text: The sheriff, district attorney, solicitor-general, court clerk, probate judge and public defender held a news conference and sent the Board a letter.
framing_issues.issue: Stated as fact with no outlet named, though the letter was never found (line 169) and the account rests on Atlanta News First (P-069). Other sentences in this entry do name their source.

framing_issues.text: Who pays: Departments and budget staff would have had less than four weeks to prepare and add every omitted request.
framing_issues.issue: Option C's only "who pays" item is a hypothetical deadline cost for a resolution already filed. It reads like a live tradeoff, and it is narrower than the fiscal "who pays" items for Options A and B.

framing_issues.text: The 2026 plan left savings about $2.8 million above the minimum reserve.
framing_issues.issue: The thin-savings figure appears only under Option A's "Who benefits", which nudges readers toward holding spending down. It is equally relevant to Option B's "Who pays" (savings), where it is not repeated.

framing_issues.text: Each of the six offices had a hearing slot
framing_issues.issue: Vague reference: card 2 never says which "six offices" (the justice offices listed at lines 78 and 169).

Unexplained terms for new readers: "FY" (fiscal year). "General Fund" (line 20) is called the biggest fund but never defined as the main day-to-day account. The county manager and chief financial officer are called "staff" without saying they are appointed, not elected. Public defender and superior court clerk are not explained.
